files.notes.md: Writes go to the primary database. HTTP200 from PUT /profile means the new profile was committed there. GET /profile normally reads a read replica, which copies committed changes asynchronously. Replication lag has no promised upper bound. A successful write followed by an old GET response does not by itself prove write loss. The next write is not needed to make replication happen. Logged-in clients may request GET /profile with X-Read-Primary: 1 to read from primary; the normal authorization check still applies. Anonymous callers cannot use this override. Primary reads can fail and no retry safety is promised. No production lag measurement is supplied. A proposal to make all reads use primary has not been implemented.

checks: 200 commit only primary, delayed replica no bound
no re-save instruction; old read not proof loss
exact header authenticated and authorized not anonymous; no proposal as implementation

files.notes.md: POST /imports requires an Idempotency-Key. Dedupe scope is project_id plus this key, and payload digest must match. For 10 minutes after first acceptance, repeating that pair with the same digest returns202 and the existing import_id, no second import. At exactly10 minutes the key record expires and the same key may create a new import. Same project/key with a different digest before expiry returns409, no new import. The same key in another project does not deduplicate. A timeout is an unknown acceptance outcome, not proof of rejection; no HTTP response is available to the timed-out client. GET /imports/{import_id} reports queued/running/finished; only finished confirms work completed. Without a known import_id, no lookup-by-key endpoint exists. This note specifies behavior, not a guaranteed safe recovery for clients that lack both an ID and the time of first acceptance. Do not recommend a new key or assume retry is safe after10 minutes. A future lookup-by-key endpoint is only proposed.
